newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast distillates weighed by lower NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast distillates weighed by lower NYMEX.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast distillates fell in quiet Monday trade, weighed by lower refined product futures, traders said.

Rising U.S. inventories and production continued to push down energy futures on NYMEX Monday, with heating oil for July delivery off 0.02 cents a gallon to 51.50 cents and July unleaded gasoline weakening 0.93 cents to 56.20 cents.
West Coast traders said the market was still weakening in the wake of Friday's NYMEX price collapse.

News that the crude unit at Atlantic Richfield's Carson, Calif., plant south of Los Angeles, spewed oil this weekend failed to push up the market, with traders unable to determine the effect on the plant' 255,000 barrel-per-day production.
ARCO was not immediately available for comment.
Traders said West Coast prices would continue to fall unless a U.S. inventory report on Tuesday showed lower suppliesin the region.
"That's the only hope we have for getting this market up," a trader said.
With little volume being traded traders offered distillates 1.50 to 3.00 cents a gallon lower.
Los Angeles cleaner-burning CARB diesel was bid and offered three cents lower Monday at 57/59 cents, while conventional low sulphur diesel was talked 53/54 cents, dealers said.
Offers for Los Angeles regular CARB-grade cleaner burning gasoline eased 1.00 cents to 58.50 cents a gallon Monday, with buyers willing to pay 57.50 cents, traders said.
Prompt regular unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles was flat at 55.50/56.50 cents.
